issues.description: Reading the entire script into RPC payload conflates two data flows; the file path was already sufficient.
issues.detail: The data structure is wrong here. The RPC already returns pipeline_package_path; bolting script_content onto the same response duplicates state that lives on disk. A separate download endpoint that streams the file given a path is the obvious composition: one tool reads, one tool serves. Pick the right data shape and the algorithm becomes obvious.

issues.description: Whole script content is carried through three layers of React state for no structural reason.
issues.detail: compiledContent now threads through DeploysProgress state, props, and DeployProgress props purely to feed a Blob at click time. That is state where a filter would do: on click, fetch from the backend by path, pipe to download. Storing arbitrary-sized file bodies in component state is the wrong data structure for a UI progress widget.

issues.description: File is opened without an explicit encoding.
issues.detail: open(script_path) relies on the platform default encoding. For a generated Python script this is usually fine, but being explicit with encoding="utf-8" makes the data contract clear and removes a portability surprise. Small change, removes a class of latent bug.

issues.description: Download icon is a clickable element but not a button; no keyboard affordance.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is the same shape as the existing anchor next to it. Either make it an <a download> like its neighbor (composition with the browser's built-in download behavior) or a real <button>. The current shape works but is inconsistent with the adjacent control and not keyboard-reachable.

issues.description: Filename fallback can produce an empty string from split('/').pop().
issues.detail: If compiledPath ends with a slash, split('/').pop() returns '' which is falsy, so the || fallback works. But the data structure to extract a basename is a path utility, not string splitting. Use a small helper; the algorithm follows from the right primitive.

review.summary: Decision label: WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE. The feature is small and useful, but it picked the wrong data flow: shipping the entire compiled script body through the RPC response and threading it through three layers of React state, when a path already exists and a download endpoint would compose cleanly with the browser's native download. Strip script_content from the RPC, add a small file-serving route, and let the anchor do the work. Minor: be explicit about encoding on file open, and make the download control match the shape of its anchor neighbor for keyboard access. The UX intent is right; the data shape is fighting it.
